# 0001 - Google Auth Origin Handling

**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-07-11
**Spec:** none - generated by pre-deploy ADR gate
**Deciders:** Codex, pending human review

## Context

The web app hit Google's `origin_mismatch` authorization error during browser Google sign-in. The app had two Google auth paths: Firebase Authentication popup/redirect and an optional direct Google Identity Services OAuth token client. The direct token client requires every browser origin to be registered in Google Cloud as an authorized JavaScript origin, which made local testing brittle when the configured origin did not match the running Vite origin.

## Decision

Use Firebase Authentication as the default browser Google sign-in path. Keep the direct Google Identity Services token flow only as an optional fallback for Calendar access-token recovery, and require the current browser origin to be explicitly listed in `VITE_GOOGLE_OAUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` before that direct flow can run.

## Consequences

Ordinary Google sign-in no longer depends on the optional Google Cloud OAuth client origin configuration. Calendar connection still has a path to request direct OAuth tokens when needed, but stale or partially configured local env values will not open Google's `origin_mismatch` page. Firebase authorized domains remain required for Firebase popup/redirect sign-in.

## Alternatives Considered

Only documenting the required Google Cloud Authorized JavaScript origins would keep the app vulnerable to stale local OAuth config. Removing the direct Google Identity Services path entirely would simplify auth, but could make Calendar access-token recovery harder if Firebase does not return an OAuth access token for the requested scope.
